"'''Rhythm of the Rain'''" is a song performed by American vocal group [[The Cascades (band)|the Cascades]], released in November 1962 in the US and on January 25, 1963 in the UK. It was written by Cascades band member John Claude Gummoe. On March 9, 1963, it rose to number 3 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], and spent two weeks at number 1 on ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''{{'}}s [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Easy Listening]] chart.<ref>{{cite book |title= Top Adult Contemporary: 1961-2001|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2002 |publisher=Record Research |page=49}}</ref> ''Billboard'' ranked the record as the number 4 song of 1963.<ref>[http://www.bobborst.com/popculture/songoftheyear/ Top 5 Songs of Each Year] Retrieved May 8, 2015</ref>

In March 1963, the song was a top 5 hit in the [[UK Singles Chart|United Kingdom]] and, in May that same year, was a number 1 single in [[Irish Singles Chart|Ireland]]. In Australia it rose to number 2. In Canada, the song was on the [[CHUM Chart]] for a total of 12 weeks and reached number 1 in February 1963.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://chumtribute.com/63-02-25-chart.jpg| title=CHUM Hit Parade - February 25, 1963}}</ref> In 1999 [[Broadcast Music, Inc.|BMI]] listed the song as the 9th most performed song on radio/TV in the 20th century.<ref name="BMI">[http://www.bmi.com/news/entry/232893 Top 100 Songs of the Century] Retrieved September 21, 2011</ref>

The Cascades' recording was used in the soundtrack of the 1979 film ''[[Quadrophenia (film)|Quadrophenia]]'', and included in its [[Quadrophenia (soundtrack)|soundtrack album]].<ref>[https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0079766/soundtrack IMDB Quadrophenia Entry ]</ref>

The song arrangement features distinctive use of a [[celesta]] played by arranger, [[Perry Botkin Jr.]]<ref>{{cite book| title=The Foundations of Rock : From "Blue Suede Shoes" to "Suite: Judy Blue Eyes": From "Blue Suede Shoes" to "Suite: Judy Blue Eyes |author=Walter Everett |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |year=2008 |isbn= 978-0-1953-1023-8 |page=77 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=p0p6jL-u3T4C&q=%22Rhythm+of+the+Rain%22+keyboards&pg=PT94}}</ref> Other musicians on the record include [[The Wrecking Crew (music)|Wrecking Crew]] members [[Hal Blaine]] on drums, [[Carol Kaye]] on bass, and [[Glen Campbell]] on guitar.<ref>{{cite web | title=Rhythm of the Rain - John Gummoe & the Cascades | url=https://www.rhythmoftherain.com/bio.html }}</ref>

The sound of rain and thunder are heard at the beginning and at the end of the song.

"Rhythm of the Rain" is a song performed by American vocal group the Cascades, released in November 1962 in the US and on January 25, 1963 in the UK. It was written by Cascades band member John Claude Gummoe. On March 9, 1963, it rose to number 3 on the Billboard Hot 100, and spent two weeks at number 1 on Billboard{{'}}s Easy Listening chart. Billboard ranked the record as the number 4 song of 1963.

In March 1963, the song was a top 5 hit in the United Kingdom and, in May that same year, was a number 1 single in Ireland. In Australia it rose to number 2. In Canada, the song was on the CHUM Chart for a total of 12 weeks and reached number 1 in February 1963. In 1999 BMI listed the song as the 9th most performed song on radio/TV in the 20th century.

The Cascades' recording was used in the soundtrack of the 1979 film Quadrophenia, and included in its soundtrack album.

The song arrangement features distinctive use of a celesta played by arranger, Perry Botkin Jr. Other musicians on the record include Wrecking Crew members Hal Blaine on drums, Carol Kaye on bass, and Glen Campbell on guitar.

The sound of rain and thunder are heard at the beginning and at the end of the song.

sections.heading: Theme
sections.wikitext: The lyrics are sung by a man whose lover has left him; the rain falling reminds him 'what a fool' he has been. He rhetorically asks the rain for answers, but ultimately he wishes it would 'go away' and let him cry alone.

The song was adapted into [[French language|French]] (under the title "En écoutant la pluie", meaning "Listening to the Rain") by [[Richard Anthony (singer)|Richard Anthony]]. It was recorded by [[Sylvie Vartan]], who released it as a [[single (music)|single]] in April 1963 as the lead off of her second studio album, ''[[Twiste et chante]]'', released that July.

According to the charts published by the U.S. magazine ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' (in its "Hits of the World" section), the song "En écoutant la pluie" reached number one in France.<ref name="Billboard 6 Jul 1963">{{cite magazine |title=Hits of the world |magazine=Billboard |date=6 July 1963 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XAsEAAAAMBAJ&q=%22Sylvie+Vartan%22+%22EN+ECOUTANT+LA+PLUIE%22&pg=PA31 |pages=31–32}}</ref><ref name="Billboard 13 Jul 1963">{{cite magazine |title=Hits of the world |magazine=Billboard |date=13 July 1963 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XQsEAAAAMBAJ&q=%22Sylvie+Vartan%22+%22EN+ECOUTANT+LA+PLUIE%22&pg=PA30 |pages=30–31}}</ref><ref name="Billboard 27 Jul 1963">{{cite magazine |title=Hits of the World |magazine=Billboard |date=27 July 1963 |url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_WgsEAAAAMBAJ|quote=Sylvie Vartan EN ECOUTANT LA PLUIE. |pages=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_WgsEAAAAMBAJ/page/n41 42]– }}</ref>

sections.heading: Other charting versions
sections.wikitext:
*Dutch teen idol [[Rob de Nijs]] covered the song in 1963 as "Ritme van de regen". Though originally a [[A-side and B-side|B side]], the song kick started his career and remains popular today.<ref>Vic van de Reijt, booklet to ''De Nederlandstalige cover top 100'', [[Universal Music Group|Universal Music]] 984 333-6</ref>
*[[Gary Lewis & the Playboys]] released a version of the song in 1969 that reached No. 63 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 chart, and No. 37 in [[RPM (magazine)|Canada]], their last charting single there.<ref>[http://musicvf.com/song.php?title=Rhythm+of+the+Rain+by+Gary+Lewis+%26+the+Playboys&id=17042 Gary Lewis & The Playboys, "Rhythm of the Rain" chart position] Retrieved May 9, 2015</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/obj/028020/f2/nlc008388.6026.pdf| title=RPM Top 100 Singles - June 16, 1969}}</ref>
*Pat Roberts released a version of the song in 1972 that reached No. 34 on the [[Hot Country Songs|Country chart]].<ref>[http://musicvf.com/song.php?title=Rhythm+of+the+Rain+by+Pat+Roberts&id=108327 Pat Roberts, "Rhythm of the Rain" chart position] Retrieved May 9, 2015</ref>
*[[Jacky Ward]] released a version of the song in 1978 that reached No. 11 on the [[Hot Country Songs|Country chart]].<ref>[http://musicvf.com/song.php?title=Rhythm+of+the+Rain+by+Jacky+Ward&id=107990 Jacky Ward, "Rhythm of the Rain" chart position] Retrieved May 9, 2015</ref>
*[[Neil Sedaka]] released a version of the song in 1984 that reached No. 37 on the [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|adult contemporary chart]].<ref>[http://musicvf.com/song.php?title=Rhythm+of+the+Rain+by+Neil+Sedaka&id=124728 Neil Sedaka, "Rhythm of the Rain" chart position] Retrieved May 9, 2015</ref>
*[[Dan Fogelberg]] released a version of the song in 1990 that reached No. 3 on the [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|adult contemporary chart]].<ref>[http://musicvf.com/song.php?title=Rhythm+of+the+Rain+by+Dan+Fogelberg&id=78438 Dan Fogelberg, "Rhythm of the Rain" chart position] Retrieved May 9, 2015</ref>
*[[Jason Donovan]] also recorded a version of the song for his 1990 album ''[[Between the Lines (Jason Donovan album)|Between the Lines]]'', and released it as the fourth single on 20 August 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Journey Through Stock Aitken Waterman: Ep 61: Hey There Lonely Girl to Rhythm Of The Rain on Apple Podcasts |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/au/podcast/ep-61-hey-there-lonely-girl-to-rhythm-of-the-rain/id1565879477?i=1000628973438 |access-date=2023-09-26 |website=Apple Podcasts |language=en-AU}}</ref> It reached number nine on the [[UK Singles Chart]] (returning him to the top 10 after his previous single "Another Night" only reached number 18),<ref>[http://musicvf.com/song.php?title=Rhythm+of+the+Rain+by+Jason+Donovan&id=21052 Jason Donovan, "Rhythm of the Rain" chart position] Retrieved May 9, 2015</ref> number six in Ireland, number 14 in the Flanders part of Belgium, number 25 in Finland, number 38 in Germany and number 44 in Australia. Reviewing the single, David Giles of ''[[Music Week]]'' said that "[[Stock Aitken Waterman|SAW]] have managed to capture some of the original charm, without damaging [Donovan's] chances of maintaining the flow of hits".<ref>{{cite magazine |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1990/MW-1990-08-25.pdf |title=Singles |first=David |last=Giles |magazine=[[Music Week]] |date=25 August 1990 |page=17 |via=World Radio History |accessdate=6 September 2023}}</ref> Donovan re-recorded the song for his 2008 album ''[[Let It Be Me (album)|Let It Be Me]]''.<!--| Misc = {{External music video|{{YouTube|2r9v5YqiTYI|"Rhythm of the Rain"}}}}-->
sections.text:
*Dutch teen idol Rob de Nijs covered the song in 1963 as "Ritme van de regen". Though originally a B side, the song kick started his career and remains popular today.
*Gary Lewis & the Playboys released a version of the song in 1969 that reached No. 63 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, and No. 37 in Canada, their last charting single there.
*Pat Roberts released a version of the song in 1972 that reached No. 34 on the Country chart.
*Jacky Ward released a version of the song in 1978 that reached No. 11 on the Country chart.
*Neil Sedaka released a version of the song in 1984 that reached No. 37 on the adult contemporary chart.
*Dan Fogelberg released a version of the song in 1990 that reached No. 3 on the adult contemporary chart.
*Jason Donovan also recorded a version of the song for his 1990 album Between the Lines, and released it as the fourth single on 20 August 1990. It reached number nine on the UK Singles Chart (returning him to the top 10 after his previous single "Another Night" only reached number 18), number six in Ireland, number 14 in the Flanders part of Belgium, number 25 in Finland, number 38 in Germany and number 44 in Australia. Reviewing the single, David Giles of Music Week said that "SAW have managed to capture some of the original charm, without damaging [Donovan's] chances of maintaining the flow of hits". Donovan re-recorded the song for his 2008 album Let It Be Me.
